examples.en: In winter the sun rises in the southeast.
A typhoon is coming up from the southeast.
My house is to the southeast of the school.

examples.ko: 이 방은 남동향이라 아침 해가 잘 들어요.
examples.en: This room faces southeast, so it gets morning sun well.
On the map, go toward the southeast.
A southeast wind is blowing, so it is humid.

explain: 방향은 보통 '남동쪽'처럼 '쪽'을 붙여 말해요. '동남'도 같은 방향이지만 '동남아시아'처럼 굳은 말은 '동남'을 써요. 집이 해가 아침에 드는 방향일 때 '남동향'이라는 말을 많이 써요.
explain_en: Directions are usually said with '쪽', as in '남동쪽'. '동남' means the same direction, but set terms like '동남아시아' use '동남'. For homes that get morning sun, '남동향' is commonly used.

examples.en: Soldiers found a tunnel in the mountains.
Moles live by digging burrows.
It was too dark and narrow inside the tunnel.
The kids play tunnel-digging in the sandbox.

examples.ko: 그 영화에는 땅굴로 탈출하는 장면이 나와요.
examples.en: That movie has a scene of escaping through a tunnel.
They open a tunnel made long ago to tourists.

explain: '터널'은 차나 기차가 다니게 산이나 땅 밑을 뚫은 큰 길이고, '땅굴'은 사람이나 동물이 땅속에 파 놓은 굴이에요. '땅굴을 파다'로 자주 써요. 뉴스에서는 군사 이야기에 '땅굴'이 자주 나와요.
explain_en: A '터널' is a large passage bored through a mountain or under the ground for cars and trains, while a '땅굴' is a hole dug into the ground by people or animals. You say '땅굴을 파다'. In the news, '땅굴' often appears in military stories.

examples.en: The boat leaves from the dock.
It takes thirty minutes by bus to get to the dock.
I had grilled fish at a restaurant in front of the dock.
Anglers are gathered at the dock.
It rained, so the dock is slippery.

examples.ko: 섬에 가려면 이 선착장에서 표를 사야 해요.
examples.en: To go to the island, you have to buy a ticket at this dock.

explain: '항구'는 큰 배가 드나드는 넓은 곳이고, '선착장'은 작은 배나 여객선이 서는 곳이에요. 섬에 갈 때 자주 듣는 말이에요. '부두'는 짐을 싣는 곳이라는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: '항구' is a large harbor for big ships, while '선착장' is where small boats and passenger ferries stop. You hear it often when going to an island. '부두' feels more like a place for loading cargo.

examples.en: Our company will be relocated next month.
The hospital was moved downtown.
The school is planned to move to a new building.
The new address is on the website.
The data is being transferred to the server.
The rights haven't been transferred yet.

explain: 사무실, 병원, 학교처럼 있던 곳이 다른 곳으로 옮겨질 때 써요. 이사한다는 뜻의 '이사하다'는 집에 쓰고, 이 말은 기관이나 자료에 어울려요. '이전'은 '지난'이라는 뜻의 다른 낱말도 있어요.
explain_en: Used when an office, hospital or school moves from one place to another. The everyday verb for moving house is for homes, while this one fits institutions and data. Note that the same sound can also be a different word meaning 'before'.

examples.ko: 타이어에서 바람이 새는 것 같아서 정비소에 갔어요.
examples.en: The tire seemed to be leaking air, so I went to the repair shop.

examples.ko: 정비소에서 점검표를 보여 주며 고칠 곳을 설명해 줬어요.
examples.en: At the shop they showed me the checklist and explained what to fix.
I heard the repair shop closes early today.

examples.ko: 이 근처에 믿을 만한 정비소가 있어요?
examples.en: Is there a trustworthy repair shop near here?

examples.ko: 정비소로 차를 끌고 가야 할 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think I have to take the car to the repair shop.

examples.ko: 정비소 앞에 수리를 기다리는 차들이 서 있어요.
examples.en: Cars waiting for repairs are lined up in front of the shop.

explain: 주로 자동차를 점검하고 고치는 곳을 말해요. '자동차 정비소'라고 자주 말하고, '카센터'도 같은 곳을 가리키는 말로 써요.
explain_en: It mainly refers to a place that inspects and repairs cars. People often say '자동차 정비소', and '카센터' is also used for the same kind of place.

examples.en: All the people on the plane got off safely.

examples.ko: 사고 버스의 탑승자 명단을 확인하고 있어요.
examples.en: We are checking the list of people on the bus in the accident.

examples.ko: 차 안 탑승자들이 놀라서 소리를 질렀어요.
examples.en: The people in the car were shocked and screamed.
A helicopter was sent out to rescue those on board the ship.
In this accident, the injuries of those on board were minor.
They handed out life jackets to those on board.

explain: '승객'은 요금을 내고 타는 손님을 말하고, 탑승자는 운전자나 승무원까지 포함해서 탄 사람 모두를 가리키는 경우가 많아요. 사고 뉴스에서 자주 들려요. '탑승하다'도 '타다'보다 딱딱하게 들려요.
explain_en: 승객 is a paying customer on board, while 탑승자 often includes the driver or crew, meaning everyone who is on board. You hear it often in accident news. 탑승하다 is also a stiffer word than 타다.
